app.how: Add input servers to receive audio, create routes to connect sources to destinations, and add output clients to send audio to your speakers. Audio flows from inputs through routes to outputs.

protocols.airplayClient: AirPlay: send audio to AirPlay speakers

servers.title: Input Servers
servers.what: Input servers receive audio from sources on your network. An AirPlay server shows up as an AirPlay speaker that your iPhone, iPad or Mac can play to. What it receives can be routed to your output clients.
servers.addHint: An input server receives audio from other devices. An AirPlay server shows up as an AirPlay speaker on your iPhone, iPad or Mac.
servers.interfaceHint: Leave empty or write "auto" to detect it. Name an interface, such as en0 or eth0, if detection picks the wrong one.
servers.deleteMessage: The input server is removed for good.

clients.title: Output Clients
clients.what: Output clients are where audio plays: the speakers and audio devices on your network. Add one for each speaker you want to control, then connect input servers to them with a route.
clients.addHint: An output client sends audio to a speaker or audio device. Find devices on your network, or set one up by hand if it isn't found.
clients.deleteMessage: The output client is removed for good.

routes.title: Audio Routes
routes.what: Routes connect input servers to output clients. A route sends what one source receives, such as an AirPlay stream, to one or more speakers. Several routes can play into the same speaker. A route plays only while it's on.
routes.addHint: A route connects an input server, where audio comes from, to one or more output clients, where it plays.
routes.destinationsHint: (where audio goes; hold Ctrl or Cmd to pick several)
routes.destinationsPick: Pick one or more output clients
routes.needDestination: Pick at least one destination client.
routes.deleteMessage: The audio route is removed for good.

discovery.selectFailed: Couldn't pick that device. Find devices again, or set it up by hand.
discovery.manualHint: Use this if your device wasn't found.

pairing.title: AirPlay Pairing
pairing.required: This Apple TV needs to be paired before it can be used. Enter the 4-digit PIN it shows on screen.
pairing.prompt: Enter the PIN your Apple TV shows
pairing.pinHelp: The 4-digit code on your Apple TV's screen
pairing.badPin: Enter the 4 digits your Apple TV shows.
pairing.noClient: There's no client to pair. Add it again.
pairing.doneMessage: The device is paired and ready to use.

matinee.title: Matinee
matinee.what: Connect Air-Mixer to your Matinee server and its players become speakers here (add an output client; Discover lists them), and Matinee inputs show up in Matinee and Home Assistant as players that play into your routes. Sign in once, the way you sign in a TV: approve the code on Matinee's /link page as an admin.
